name: One Day Secular Meditation Retreat in Wellington
venue: 31 Lawson Place, Mount Victoria, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
We know from ancient wisdom and modern psychology that meditation brings many benefits for our mental and physical wellbeing. It can reduce worry and pain, and improve calmness, focus, sleep, relationships and life satisfaction. The more time we spend meditating, and the more skilled we become, the greater the benefits.

So take a restorative break from your daily life, meet other meditators, and strengthen your practice at this small-group retreat. Everyone is welcome, whatever their level of meditation experience or preferred style. The retreat is beginner-friendly, and our approach is secular (meaning non-religious) which makes room for diverse beliefs.

The programme

We will begin with introductions, followed by a guided meditation that covers the core skills of both sitting and walking meditation. For the rest of the day, the meditation will be unguided apart from occasional bells to announce breaks, and to remind you to alternate between sitting and walking (if that's what you choose to do).

To help quieten the mind, many participants prefer not to talk again until the discussion circle at the end of the retreat. However some people like to chat with others during the breaks, and there is space allocated for this. The retreat leaders are always available for quiet conversations if you need support with your practice.

The venue

The Innermost Gardens hall is nestled between the central city suburb of Mount Victoria and the green town belt. This provides a peaceful nature-rich setting for the retreat, surrounded by community gardens to enjoy during the breaks or walking meditation.

There will be hot drinks and snacks available throughout the day. For lunch the participants bring a plate of vegetarian food to share. The venue has a full kitchen including cutlery, plates, bowls, fridge, stove, and a microwave.

The leaders

Bryan Royds is an adult educator and registered counsellor with a passion for wellbeing science and leadership development. He has been meditating and teaching meditation skills in groups for many years, including the well-researched methods of Mindfulness Based Stress Reduction (MBSR).

Sarah Jane Barnett is a writer and creative writing teacher at Massey University. She has been a Buddhist for ten years, practicing mostly Vipassana meditation. She also co-facilitates a meditation group for people who practice Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (an evidence-based modern psychotherapy and wellbeing method).

The registration fee is only $40 for waged and $20 for unwaged, fully refundable until one day prior.

Concession $30 (early bird concession price $27 until midnight 29 Nov)

Nota Bene presents: Christmas Fantasia

From centuries-old texts to traditional carols given new musical life, this concert explores the many ways composers across different eras and cultures have interpreted the Christmas story.

Our programme brings together music from England to Appalachia, with works by Vaughan Williams, Warlock, Dalglish and Ešenvalds. The music ranges from reflective settings and rich harmonies to folk-inspired carols and familiar Christmas melodies.

Vaughan Williams’ Fantasia on Christmas Carols weaves together traditional English carol melodies, some emerging in the choir and others in the accompaniment. In contrast, Malcolm Dalglish’s Star in the East sets three Appalachian Christmas songs for choir and harp, drawing on a different folk tradition.

Joined by baritone Joe Haddow, harpist Michelle Velvin and organist Rachel Malcolm-Swindells, Nota Bene presents a programme that moves between familiar carols and less familiar musical settings.

And what better way to finish than by singing some favourite Christmas carols together? As is our tradition, we hope you’ll stay and join us for refreshments after the concert.

Rachel Malcolm-Swindells - Organ

Michelle Velvin - Harp

Joe Haddow - Baritone

Intimate Earth celebrates ways of seeing in distinction to dominant modes of audio-visual media in the twenty-first century. name: Welcome Space Brothers - The Extraordinary True Story of the Unarius Academy of Science
venue: 93 Mornington Road, Brooklyn, Wellington 6021, New Zealand
long_description:
WELCOME SPACE BROTHERS is a documentary that dives into the extraordinary true story of the Unarius Academy of Science, an extraterrestrial-channeling spiritual school founded in El Cajon in the 1970s. Led by the dazzlingly outlandish Ruth E. Norman—revered as "Archangel Uriel"—Unarius evolved into a wildly inventive public-access television phenomenon. The group produced films that appeared to be elaborately campy space epics yet were, at their core, sincere therapeutic works. 

From The Source Family director Jodi Wille comes another mind-expanding voyage into the wild frontiers of American belief, bringing her singular blend of empathy, humor, and emotional insight to one of the country's most fascinating outsider communities. Produced by Caryn Capotosto (Won’t You Be My Neighbor) and Jodi Wille. Executive producers include Elijah Wood, Moby, and Oscar-winning filmmakers Phil Lord and Christopher Miller.

Please join us for the Wellington screening of WELCOME SPACE BROTHERS - brought to you by Erika Grant and Night Church Cinema. This is a dress up event - come dressed in your favorite UFO/Cult fit. There will be prizes for best dressed, and DJ's Oona Verse and Martyn Pepperell plus others will guide us into the wild starry night with space cult inspired dance tracks.

The bar and restaurant will be open for dinner and drinks. This is a one off event, not to be missed!!

“Wild and Very Trippy” - Jodi Wille

“If I didn’t know Jodi Wille’s film, Welcome Space Brothers, was a documentary, I’d swear it was a WTF, insane, sci-fi tale of weirdness. The story of Ruth is fascinating…..” - Alan NG, Film Threat 

“It’s a vision of healing, acceptance, peace, cooperation, and hope, expressed through an outpouring of unbridled creative energy. If that spells crazy, beam me up!” — Doug Harvey, Artillery

name: Film screening and kōrero with Other Cinemas
venue: Wallace Street, Mount Cook, Wellington, New Zealand
long_description:
Join us for a special free screening of I Carry It With Me Everywhere by Other Cinemas and The Neglected Miracle by Barry Barclay at Massey University, with kōrero from Arwa Aburawa, Turab Shah, and Hana Pera Aoake on Monday 9 November 6:15pm-9pm.

I Carry It With Me Everywhere was informed by interviews with first-generation migrants living in the UK. This short film weaves together the lives of multiple characters as they confront inherited ideas of belonging. The Neglected Miracle is a film that forms the culmination of five years of international research into the question of who owns our seeds. This involves interviews with corporations, scientists and everyday farmers in the developing world. This was shot over two years in eight different countries. 

We are very lucky to be joined by Turab Shah and Arwa Aburawa of Other Cinemas for a kōrero before the screening. They have come all the way from the UK, so don't miss this chance to hear about the film directly from its makers!

This screening is programmed in concert with the exhibition Unseen. Unheard. Unarchived. by Other Cinemas and Friends, curated by Hana Pera Aoake. The exhibition is on at Enjoy until 19 December.

Snacks and drinks provided!

The screening will be held at Massey Cinema, Old Dominion Museum Building (East entrance): 15 Buckle Street, Mount Cook, Wellington

(Block 10 Tokomaru, Pukeahu Mount Cook, Wellington)

This event is supported by Toi Rauwhārangi College of Creative Arts, Massey University. Enjoy's Public Engagement programme is made possible by the support of Wellington City Council.

The Neglected Miracle

Film by Barry Barclay. Narrated by Keri Kaa. A Pacific films production. Film courtesy of Aotearoa New Zealand Film Heritage Trust – Te Puna Ataata (ANZFHT) and Ngā Taonga (NT). Festivals: 1985 Wellington Film Festival (World Premiere), 1985 London Film Festival, 2009 NZ International Film Festival, 2013 imagineNATIVE (Toronto).

long_description:
We have a very special event to close the year.

WIFT NZ is delighted to welcome Oscar and BAFTA-winning costume designer Kate Hawley.

This year, Kate has won the following awards for her contribution to Guillermo del Toro's Frankenstein (2025)

Academy Award for Best Achievement in Costume Design

BAFTA for Best Costume Design

Critics Choice for Best Costume Design

Costume Designers Guild Awards for Excellence in Period Film

Plus 19 other awards around the globe!

She also received multiple nominations for Best Costume for Lord Of The Rings: Rings of Power (2022) and Crimson Peak (2015).

To top it all off, she also received the inaugural Costume Designer of the Year Award from the British Fashion Council. 

Hawley has been praised for her "...meticulous construction, narrative sensitivity and ability to elevate character through custom-built textiles and silhouettes. ...she has built an international career across film, opera, theatre and ballet. Her credits span Crimson Peak and Pacific Rim to Suicide Squad, Edge of Tomorrow and The Hobbit. Her work has previously earned an Emmy nomination, a Costume Designers Guild Award and Saturn and Empire award" - (Fashion United UK)

Kate’s body of work speaks for itself. She’s another fantastic story of a career that started at home in Aotearoa and went global,

We’ll pick her brain (not in a Frankenstein way) about her career, her craft, and what it takes to build a whole world out of fabric, dye and attention to detail. Moderated by Robin Laing.

Date: Tuesday 17th November

Time: Drinks from 6pm | Talk 6:30-8pm

Location: Wētā Workshop Space, 129 Park Road, Miramar, Wellington

WIFT Members free, non-members $25. Drinks and nibbles provided.

name: 2026 Korea Wellington Business Breakfast
venue: 2 Harris Street, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Mark 10 years since the formal city-to-city partnership between Wellington and its sister city Seoul, with Korean and New Zealand business leaders, officials and organisations over a Korean-inspired breakfast.

Description:

The Embassy of the Republic of Korea, Wellington City Council and the Korea New Zealand Business Council (KNZBC) are pleased to invite you to the 2026 Korea Wellington Business Breakfast.

Seoul is Wellington’s sister city, and this year marks 10 years since the formal city-to-city partnership was established during an official mayoral visit, further strengthening the relationship between our two cities. The breakfast brings together Korean and New Zealand businesses, organisations and officials to explore the opportunities shaping the relationship between our two countries, from trade and investment to primary industries, infrastructure and the creative sector.

Held in Te Akapuanga o Waimānga, the Māori whare within the Wellington City Council building, the morning will open with a karakia and mihimihi. This is followed by remarks from Wellington City Council and the Korean Ambassador, a keynote address from Deer Industry New Zealand, and a panel discussion with business leaders sharing practical experiences of working with Korea, including Q&A.

Guests will enjoy a breakfast with a Korean twist alongside tea and coffee.

This is a great opportunity to connect with others who share an interest in the continued growth of the New Zealand–Korea relationship. We look forward to welcoming you.

long_description:
This workshop will demonstrate the very basics of Tukutuku where each participant will come away with a form of Tukutuku and knowledge to inspire their own mahi toi. 

All materials supplied. Prior to the workshop participants are encouraged to research Tukutuku patterns and become familiar with the meanings.

 

Artist biography.
Elena Rei
Ngāti Toarangatira, Ngāruahine, Ngāti Koata, Ngāti Tama, Sāmoa 

Elena Rei’s creative practice sits within the realm of Te Whare Pora, weaving together customary and contemporary processes of raranga, whatu muka and tukutuku. Interlaced throughout her works are collective dreams, moments of remembering and profound experiences with the materials she uses. Much of Elena’s practice is intuitive, emulating the ways of her tūpuna and drawing from a visual language that has been woven through time. Her works reimage and make familiar our inherent connection to ngā atua wāhine, through themes of aroha, grief, whakapapa and reconnection. 

Elena studied design and textiles at Massey University, where she gained early insights into practices within Te Whare Pora. A formative experience during this time was learning tukutuku under the guidance of Kohai Grace during classes at Whitireia, an experience that continues to inform her practice today.

Nota Bene presents: Christmas Fantasia

From centuries-old texts to traditional carols given new musical life, this concert explores the many ways composers across different eras and cultures have interpreted the Christmas story.

Our programme brings together music from England to Appalachia, with works by Vaughan Williams, Warlock, Dalglish and Ešenvalds. The music ranges from reflective settings and rich harmonies to folk-inspired carols and familiar Christmas melodies.

Vaughan Williams’ Fantasia on Christmas Carols weaves together traditional English carol melodies, some emerging in the choir and others in the accompaniment. In contrast, Malcolm Dalglish’s Star in the East sets three Appalachian Christmas songs for choir and harp, drawing on a different folk tradition.

Joined by baritone Joe Haddow, harpist Michelle Velvin and organist Rachel Malcolm-Swindells, Nota Bene presents a programme that moves between familiar carols and less familiar musical settings.

And what better way to finish than by singing some favourite Christmas carols together? As is our tradition, we hope you’ll stay and join us for refreshments after the concert.

Rachel Malcolm-Swindells - Organ

Michelle Velvin - Harp

Joe Haddow - Baritone

venue: 12 Cambridge Terrace, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Described by the 2026 Arts Foundation Te Tumu Toi Laureate panel as "without a doubt one of New Zealand's most important living writers", internationally bestselling author Catherine Chidgey returns to Verb to discuss her tenth enthralling novel. The Starving Bride is an urgent and searing story set in near-future England.


Dumped by her boyfriend, fired from her job and estranged from her parents, Hazel Whitlock signs up for a sideshow act in Blackpool. The seaside resort has revived all the cancelled old favourites and she will be the Starving Bride. On display in the iconic Blackpool Tower, with a ravenous lion prowling the enclosure, Hazel must lie in silence while strangers view her body.

Join Catherine and Kate Camp for a special one-night event as they discuss the many layers of The Starving Bride, writing female experiences and the questions the book raises about spectacle, desire, survival and society's obsession with beauty.

Unity Books will be at the event bookselling and Catherine will be book signing.

Cover artwork by Max Thompson. Cover design by Todd Atticus. Author photo by Ebony Lamb.

Catherine Chidgey’s novels have been published to international acclaim. Her first, In a Fishbone Church, won Best First Book at the New Zealand Book Awards and at the Commonwealth Writers’ Prize (South East Asia and South Pacific). In the UK it won the Betty Trask Award and was longlisted for the Orange Prize.

Her second, Golden Deeds, was a Notable Book of the Year in the New York Times Book Review and a Best Book in the LA Times. Catherine has won the Prize in Modern Letters, the Katherine Mansfield Award, the Katherine Mansfield Fellowship, the Janet Frame Fiction Prize, and, for her 2016 novel The Wish Child, the Acorn Foundation Fiction Prize.

Her 2020 novel, Remote Sympathy, was shortlisted for the DUBLIN Literary Award and the Jann Medlicott Acorn Prize for Fiction, and was longlisted for the Women’s Prize for Fiction. The Axeman’s Carnival (2022) won the Jann Medlicott Acorn Prize for Fiction. Catherine's two most recent novels are the critically acclaimed Pet (2023) and The Book of Guilt (2025), also published by John Murray.

Catherine lectures in Creative Writing at the University of Waikato.

Kate Camp is the author of many collections of poems, including The Mirror of Simple Annihilated Souls (winner of the 2011 NZ Post Book Award for Poetry) and How to Be Happy Though Human: New and Selected Poems (2020), and a collection of essays, You Probably Think This Song Is About You (2022). Her most recent book is Makeshift Seasons (2025), a new collection of poetry. Kate was born in 1972 and lives in Wellington.

long_description:
Join us for a special evening celebrating the creativity, achievements and unique perspectives of young photographers from across the Wellington region and beyond.

Following the success of our inaugural awards in 2025, which brought together nearly 200 children, families, photographers and supporters, the Young Photographer Awards are returning for another inspiring celebration!

Organised by The Art of Seeing Academy, the awards recognise young people aged 7–18 who have participated in our photography workshops throughout the year.

For many of these young photographers, this may be the first time their work has been publicly celebrated. Every photograph tells a story, and every young photographer brings a different way of seeing the world.

What to expect on the night

This year's ceremony will bring together young photographers, their families, professional photographers and our wider creative community.

The evening will feature:

Young Photographer Awards presentation: Celebrating selected young photographers and recognising their creativity, effort and achievements.

Five inspiring guest speakers: Professional photographers sharing their experiences, creative journeys and stories from behind the lens.

Young photographers' work: A celebration of the images, ideas and perspectives developed through our workshops.

A community celebration: An opportunity to come together, support young talent and recognise the importance of creativity in young people's lives.

Meet our guest speakers

We are delighted to welcome five professional photographers who will share their experiences, insights and stories with our young creatives

Fairlie Atkinson
Photography in service of our community


Fairlie is a photography teacher at Kāpiti College who has helped students achieve national recognition through awards and exhibitions. Passionate about creativity and community, she encourages young photographers to use their images to tell meaningful stories, advocate for causes they care about and make a positive difference.

Tara Swan
Wildlife photography and conservation


Tara is a wildlife photographer and ecologist with over a decade of experience working with rare birds. Her photography focuses on Aotearoa's native wildlife and Kaimanawa horses. She'll share how photography can tell the stories of our natural world and inspire greater care for wildlife and conservation.

Dave Allen
Overcoming self-doubt in photography

With over 30 years of experience in photography and videography, Dave will explore how to build confidence as a photographer. He'll share insights into managing self-doubt, stepping outside your comfort zone and recognising the creative strengths that come with being yourself.

Stephen Garner
Projects, corgis, and people: How I get unstuck when I don't know what to photograph

Stephen has been taking photographs since receiving his first camera at age six. He loves street, travel and documentary photography, often accompanied by his two wind-up corgis, Dante and Virgil. He'll share his playful approach to finding inspiration and overcoming creative blocks.

Emmeline Plachecki
Beyond the lens: The stories, feelings and connections behind equine photography

Emmeline is a New Zealand photographer specialising in equine photography. Combining her understanding of horses with a creative eye, she captures the emotions, personalities and connections that make each horse unique. She'll explore how photography can tell stories that go beyond what we see.

Every young photographer deserves to be seen

Throughout 2026, The Art of Seeing Academy has continued to introduce children and teenagers to photography through hands-on workshops across the Lower North Island region.

Some participants pick up a camera for the first time. Others return to develop their skills, explore new ideas and discover their own photographic style.

Our workshops encourage young people to slow down, observe their surroundings, express themselves and build confidence through creativity. We welcome young people of all abilities, backgrounds and learning needs.

The Young Photographer Awards are an opportunity to recognise their progress and celebrate what they have achieved.

Come and celebrate with us!

Whether you are a parent, a young photographer, a photography enthusiast or simply someone who believes in supporting young creative talent, we would love to see you there.

Join us for an evening of inspiring stories, wonderful photographs and well-deserved recognition for our next generation of photographers.

long_description:
Home Alone Music is proud to announce the Aotearoa and Australian tour in celebration of Timothy Blackman's new album 'Between the Islands' (HAM050) in January/February 2027.  

In Aotearoa, there will be full band shows in Wellington and Palmerston North. 

For the full band shows, Timothy's backing band will consist of Tessa Dillion on bass/backing vocals (Mystery Waitress and Tessa de Lyon) and Olivia Campion on drums (Mystery Waitress and Yumi Zouma).

Between the Islands was recorded with a live studio band consisting of Blackman, Tessa Dillon (Mystery Waitress), and Hikurangi Schaverien-Kaa (French for Rabbits, Dateline). Lee Prebble recorded and mixed their performances at The Surgery Recording Studio in Omāroro, Newtown, Wellington over three days in May 2025. Additional overdubs were performed and recorded by Blackman’s longtime collaborator Brooke Singer (French for Rabbits) at her home in Wellington. The album was mastered by Carl Saff in Chicago, Illinois.  Album artwork by Alex Thornton.  


----

Timothy Blackman is a Te Whanganui-a-Tara Wellington based singer-songwriter, recording artist and founder of independent Aotearoa New Zealand record label Home Alone.

Since his first EP in 2006, Blackman has released a string of acclaimed records such as Modern Sprawl, I've Never Lived, Everyone Needs Something to Hold On To and Brightest Days. Blackman grew up in the Wellington region, began playing violin at five and guitar at ten, and was performing in bands around the Lower Hutt/Wellington area as a teenager. 

His music has since taken him from the bedrooms and small venues of Aotearoa to stages across Europe, the UK, United States and Australia, where he has performed alongside artists including The Mountain Goats and Scout Niblett. His music sits in an intimate space, flitting somewhere between the introspective songwriting of Bill Callahan and Bonnie Prince Billy, and the DIY spirit of New Zealand icon Chris Knox. His songs are personal and unvarnished: thoughtful, melancholic and often quietly funny, with a fascination for place, memory, displacement and the strange details of everyday life.

Join us for a special free screening of I Carry It With Me Everywhere by Other Cinemas and The Neglected Miracle by Barry Barclay at Massey University, with kōrero from Arwa Aburawa, Turab Shah, and Hana Pera Aoake on Monday 9 November 6:15pm-9pm.

I Carry It With Me Everywhere was informed by interviews with first-generation migrants living in the UK. This short film weaves together the lives of multiple characters as they confront inherited ideas of belonging. The Neglected Miracle is a film that forms the culmination of five years of international research into the question of who owns our seeds. This involves interviews with corporations, scientists and everyday farmers in the developing world. This was shot over two years in eight different countries. 

We are very lucky to be joined by Turab Shah and Arwa Aburawa of Other Cinemas for a kōrero before the screening. They have come all the way from the UK, so don't miss this chance to hear about the film directly from its makers!

This screening is programmed in concert with the exhibition Unseen. Unheard. Unarchived. by Other Cinemas and Friends, curated by Hana Pera Aoake. The exhibition is on at Enjoy until 19 December.

Snacks and drinks provided!

The screening will be held at Massey Cinema, Old Dominion Museum Building (East entrance): 15 Buckle Street, Mount Cook, Wellington

(Block 10 Tokomaru, Pukeahu Mount Cook, Wellington)

This event is supported by Toi Rauwhārangi College of Creative Arts, Massey University. Enjoy's Public Engagement programme is made possible by the support of Wellington City Council.

The Neglected Miracle

Film by Barry Barclay. Narrated by Keri Kaa. A Pacific films production. Film courtesy of Aotearoa New Zealand Film Heritage Trust – Te Puna Ataata (ANZFHT) and Ngā Taonga (NT). Festivals: 1985 Wellington Film Festival (World Premiere), 1985 London Film Festival, 2009 NZ International Film Festival, 2013 imagineNATIVE (Toronto).

Philip Whitmore, Partner, Cyber and Digital at KPMG

Tristana also just scooped up the TUANZ Member awards for 'Outstanding Future Leader'.

The legendary “Mysticssippi Blues Man” returns to New Zealand in 2027 with his extraordinary fusion of blues and Indian classical music — and his brand new album, Falling Upwards.

✨ Family friendly

ABOUT HARRY MANX

Canadian musician Harry Manx has created one of the most distinctive sounds in roots music, blending deep blues, hypnotic grooves and the spiritual depth of Indian classical music into something entirely his own.

Moving effortlessly between slide guitar, harmonica, banjo and the remarkable 20-stringed Mohan Veena, Harry creates a live show that shifts from raw, earthy blues to something soulful, cinematic and completely transporting.

“A seamless fit between blues and Indian classical music” — DownBeat Magazine

THE FALLING UPWARDS TOUR

In 2027, rather than the noise and distance of a large concert venue, these performances are designed to be experienced up close — in intimate listening rooms where every note, story and subtlety can be heard.

For longtime fans, it's a chance to reconnect with an extraordinary artist. For those discovering Harry for the first time, it's an introduction to a musical world unlike anything else.

For one special evening, Old St Paul's becomes an intimate listening room, bringing world-class music to town!

🎟️ TICKETS ON SALE NOW!

Following a completely sold-out New Zealand tour, Harry Manx returns for another extraordinary afternoon of intimate live music.

With limited seating available at Old St Paul's we recommend booking early to avoid disappointment.

Don't miss your chance to experience the remarkable Harry Manx LIVE in Wellington!

From crystal-clear tropical reefs and wild coastlines to towering waves and the depths of the open ocean, these beautifully crafted films showcase the ocean from every perspective. long_description:
KIM CHURCHILL LIVE IN WELLINGTON!

One man. A guitar, harmonica, percussion and an extraordinary voice. A whole world of sound.

Australian singer-songwriter and multi-instrumentalist Kim Churchill returns to New Zealand for a very special evening of world-class live music at the beautiful Old St Paul's!

From the legendary stages of Glastonbury and the Montreal Jazz Festival to intimate venues around the world, Kim has built an international reputation for his captivating one-man-band performances, incredible guitar playing and heartfelt songwriting.

Blending folk, blues, roots and indie music, Kim creates a remarkable live experience. Intricate fingerpicking, rhythmic guitar percussion, harmonica, foot drums and soaring vocals somehow come together through just one performer.

His much-loved song Window to the Sky went platinum in Australia, and his music has reached millions of listeners around the world.

But it's on stage where Kim Churchill truly comes alive. His shows move from explosive, foot-stomping energy to beautifully intimate moments, with warmth, humour and stories from a lifetime spent travelling the world playing music.

Whether you're already a fan or discovering Kim for the first time, this is a concert not to be missed!

CONCERT DETAILS

📍 Old St Paul's, Wellington

📅 24 February 2027

🚪 Doors open 7:00pm

🎶 Concert starts 7:30pm

✨ Fully seated, intimate listening-room concert

ABOUT KIM CHURCHILL

Raised in the coastal town of Merimbula, Australia, Kim Churchill began his musical journey as a young busker before setting off around the world with a guitar, a surfboard and a remarkable talent for songwriting.

After winning the Byron Bay Bluesfest busking competition, Kim went on to perform at major international festivals, share stages with celebrated musicians and build a devoted global audience.

His distinctive one-man-band style is something that really needs to be seen to be believed. Combining technically brilliant acoustic guitar work with percussion, harmonica and a powerful, expressive voice, Kim creates a sound far bigger than one person should be capable of.

Yet beyond the extraordinary musicianship lies a gifted songwriter whose music reflects a lifelong love of travel, nature, connection and the freedom of the open road.

ABOUT THE VENUE

In the heart of Wellington, Old St Paul's is one of New Zealand's most breathtaking heritage venues, renowned for its magnificent timber architecture, soaring vaulted ceilings and extraordinary atmosphere.

For one night, Nightingale Concerts brings its intimate listening-room experience to this iconic former church, offering audiences the chance to enjoy a remarkable Australian touring artist in one of Wellington's most beautiful and historic settings.

Expect an evening of exceptional music, heartfelt songs, extraordinary guitar playing and the kind of connection that makes live performance so special.

🎟️ TICKETS ARE ON SALE NOW!

From international festival stages to intimate concert halls around the world, Kim Churchill has captivated audiences with his extraordinary live performances.

Don't miss your chance to experience him up close in Wellington. Secure your tickets today!

long_description:
A Deep Listening Soundbath inside the sublime acoustics of Erskine Chapel

$45

Limited door sales for $50

Please bring a yoga mat, pillow, eye mask and blanket - or whatever it is you need to feel most warm and comfortable. Dress comfortably.

Discover the transformative effects of sound therapy with this 1.5hr-hour sound bath experience.

During this session, participants will be surrounded by the resonant vibrations of gongs and taonga pūoro, carefully designed to induce deep states of relaxation and calm. As you settle into the experience, allow the soothing tones to wash over you, releasing tension and promoting a sense of inner peace.

Scientific studies have highlighted the benefits of sound therapy in reducing stress and promoting overall well-being. The rhythmic patterns and overtones of the gongs and other instruments can help entrain brainwaves, leading to a meditative state and improved mental clarity.

Beyond the immediate effects, many participants report experiencing lasting benefits such as improved sleep, reduced anxiety, and enhanced mood following a gong bath session. By immersing yourself in the healing vibrations of the sounds, you can tap into a deeper sense of relaxation and rejuvenation.

Whether you're looking to unwind after a long day or explore new avenues of self-care, this 1.5hr-hour soundbath offers a unique opportunity to reconnect with yourself and find balance amidst the hustle and bustle of daily life. There will be cups of tea available afterwards to help us integrate and ground.

*THIS EVENT IS RESTRICTED TO 40 PEOPLE ONLY**

Disclaimer
Sound baths are safe and supportive for most people. However, please consult your doctor or mental health professional before attending if you:-have a pacemaker or other implanted medical device
-live with epilepsy or a sound-sensitive condition
-are in the first trimester of pregnancy
-are experiencing severe or unmanaged mental health challenges (such as psychosis, schizophrenia, or PTSD)If you have recent injuries, surgeries, or other health concerns, let me know so we can make sure you’re comfortable.

Everyone responds differently to sound. If at any point during the session you feel overwhelmed or uncomfortable, you are welcome to sit up, move gently, or step outside. Your wellbeing always comes first

About Us

Briar Prastiti

Greek–New Zealand composer and vocalist Briar Prastiti is known for her diverse musical practice, spanning contemporary orchestral and chamber music, film, theatre, songwriting, and electronic production. Her most recent compositional project was an epic work for massed choir, solo voice, and taonga pūoro, commissioned for the opening ceremony of Te Matapihi ki te Ao Nui, Wellington Central Library. In this work, Briar performed as solo vocalist alongside Alistair Fraser on taonga pūoro. 

Alistair Fraser

Alistair is a practitioner of ngā taonga pūoro. He has performed, composed, and collaborated with many of Aotearoa's finest artists, across genres of music and alongside various artistic disciplines since 1999. He worked as a maker, researcher and performer of ngā taonga pūoro nationally and internationally for the past 26 years. He has toured as a soloist with the New Zealand Symphony Orchestra, worked recently with Good Company Arts, Shayne Carter with the Zealand Dance Company for their work Home, Land and Sea, and also for David Long and Stephen Gallagher's score for the Emmy Award winning TV series Secrets at Red Rocks.

Erika Grant

Erika is a musician and astrologer based in Te Whanganui-a-Tara. She has 35+ years musical experience, in bands, orchestras and various ensembles. She has created music for film, parades and overnight soundbaths. Erika has an interest in the healing properties of sound for mental and physical wellbeing, which she currently explores through her gong bathing practice

If you’re new here, welcome - stoked you found us!

We’re tipsy trails. We’re on a mission to get more people in their 20s outdoors and turn an online community into a seriously epic in-person one.

We walk together along some of New Zealand’s most stunning trails, chatting with new and old mates - usually wrapping things up with a well-earned beverage afterwards.

We’re a club built on the idea that getting outdoors doesn’t have to be super serious or intense - it should be accessible, with a bit of fun. You don’t need fancy gear. You don’t need to be “outdoorsy.” You don’t even need a group to come with - rocking up solo is totally normal here. All paces and abilities are welcome. You just need to show up and enjoy the rest.

So, what do you say? Put down your phone and come outside with us.

Trail: Skyline Track, Johnsonville

Length: Out & back (halfway), approx. 12km, 460m elevation gain, around 3 hours

Difficulty: Rated Moderate by AllTrails

Water bottle (make sure it’s full!)

comfy walking shoes,

a warm layer for during and after the hike 🧥,

a waterproof jacket (just in case 🌧️),

trail snacks (interpret this however your heart desires),

hat, sunglasses, and sunscreen (fingers crossed for sunshine ☀️),

a bag to throw everything in (backpack or side bag works perfectly 🎒)

📍 MEETING POINT

Meeting details and timing will be emailed once you’ve registered.

Keep an eye on our Instagram and tipsy trails Facebook messenger group chats for any updates or weather changes.

🍻 POST-HIKE PLANS?

With the trail wrapped up and the afternoon still ahead, we’ll head to a nearby pub for a well-earned beverage and bite to eat!


🚙 NEED / CAN OFFER A LIFT

Carpooling is available for anyone who needs a lift or can offer one. Once you have registered, you can connect with others in the Facebook messenger carpool group chat, share your area, and organise pick-up details directly.

🥾 REGISTRATION

This is a free community event with limited spots. Registration is required.

Got questions? Our DM’s are always open on Instagram @tipsy_____________

long_description:
Jazz and Beyond for students 19 and under

December 14–17, 2026

Coordinated by Chris Beernink, Dave Wilson, Daniel Hayles, Andrew Faleatua, Lance Philip. Proudly supported by the Tauranga Jazz Society.

Take it to the next level as a player or vocalist at the Jazz and Beyond Workshops! Young musicians from across Aotearoa come together to dive into jazz and connected styles, working closely with some of the country’s leading performers and educators. In a friendly, inclusive environment, you’ll grow your skills, make new musical connections, and learn alongside other students your age from all around the motu.

Here’s what’s in store:

small group ensembles led by professional musicians

developing improvisation skills in supportive settings

an introduction to music production

listening sessions that expand your skills

inclusive jam sessions where all are welcome

ensemble performances at the end of week concert

And more!

If you're 19 or under with at least a year of experience on your instrument or in vocal training, you’re welcome to join. Choose from trumpet, trombone, saxophone, clarinet, flute, bass, piano, guitar, drums, vibraphone, or voice.

The workshops are held at the New Zealand School of Music–Te Kōkī at Te Herenga Waka-Victoria University of Wellington. Follow the Jazz and Beyond Workshops on Instagram or Facebook for the latest updates. Email jazzandbeyondworkshops@gmail.com with any questions.

Schedule

The workshops run 9:00am-4:30pm Monday through Thursday, with evening activities including concerts and our inclusive jam sessions Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday. Students perform in a closing concert on Thursday afternoon.

Accommodation

Students arrange their own accommodation. Often students from outside Wellington stay together in groups with a parent chaperone. Options for housing near Victoria University of Wellington include backpacker hostels and hotels. If you have a group of 15 or more, University Student Housing may be an option. Email jazzandbeyondworkshops@gmail.com if you'd like to pursue this option.

Meals

Lunch for the four days is available for purchase at many convenient locations on campus, or students may bring their own lunch.

Equipment

Provided equipment includes drum kits, guitar and bass amps, pianos/keyboards, microphones and PAs for vocalists.

All brass and wind players should bring their own instruments.

Drummers: you are required to bring your own cymbals, sticks, and hi-hat clutch.

Guitarists and bass players: you are required to bring your own instruments as well as cables (leads).

Preparation

All students with one year of experience on an instrument or in vocal training have the skills required to participate, so no musical preparation is required. On the first day, students will play a very short audition to be placed in an appropriate ensemble. Guidelines for this short audition will be sent to all registered participants in advance of the workshops.

Cost

Early bird price: $325 - register before 19th October

Standard price $350 - on or after 19th October

Registration is open to all until all spots are filled.

We are dedicated to ensuring all students can participate in the workshops without financial constraints. If the cost poses a barrier, please email us at jazzandbeyondworkshops@gmail.com and we will find a solution to facilitate your participation!

Make an evening of it and come for a late afternoon drink and repas (meal : ) and get into the groove when the beats start.
Early doors, early night.

If you’re new here, welcome - stoked you found us!

We’re tipsy trails. We’re on a mission to get more people in their 20s outdoors and turn an online community into a seriously epic in-person one.

We walk together along some of New Zealand’s most stunning trails, chatting with new and old mates - usually wrapping things up with a well-earned beverage afterwards.

We’re a club built on the idea that getting outdoors doesn’t have to be super serious or intense - it should be accessible, with a bit of fun. You don’t need fancy gear. Water bottle (make sure it’s full!)

comfy walking shoes,

a warm layer for during and after the hike 🧥,

a waterproof jacket (just in case 🌧️),

trail snacks (interpret this however your heart desires),

hat, sunglasses, and sunscreen (fingers crossed for sunshine ☀️),

a bag to throw everything in (backpack or side bag works perfectly 🎒)

Meeting details and timing will be emailed once you’ve registered.

Keep an eye on our Instagram and tipsy trails Facebook messenger group chats for any updates or weather changes.

With the trail wrapped up and the afternoon still ahead, we’ll head to a nearby pub for a well-earned beverage and bite to eat!


🚙 NEED / CAN OFFER A LIFT

Carpooling is available for anyone who needs a lift or can offer one. Once you have registered, you can connect with others in the Facebook messenger carpool group chat, share your area, and organise pick-up details directly.

This is a free community event with limited spots. Registration is required.

Got questions? Our DM’s are always open on Instagram @tipsy_____________

Haere mai for the cheekiest fundraiser known to femmes/thems - Butch Auction 2026 🔥

A handful of butches are donating their services to fundraise for InsideOUT Kōaro and Gender Minorities Aotearoa. The services range from chefs, barbers, writing workshop facilitator, waiata performer, cocktail bartender etc,

Here's what you need to know before you come along, during the auction, and what happens afterwards.

Before the Auction -

Butch profiles will be uploaded on this event page and 04BC instagram page so you know who you'd want to bid for. The profiles will show terms and conditions such as

if the service is available for a group setting,

how long is the offer valid for,

additional costs may apply to certain services;
For example, you bid on a chef and win (congrats!). You have your first sit down and plan out a 3-course meal for a special event for you and 4 other friends. The chef may only offer to cover the first $100 of the groceries so you will need to reimburse them for the rest of the grocery bill.

how much notice to give your butch before redeeming the service,

any other conditions or boundaries attached to the offer.

Make yourself a paddle to use on the night for bidding purposes only, if you don't have a ready-to-go one. Please do not use the paddle on anything or anyone at the event, even if it was consented! This is not the space for it.

Please consider what you are comfortable paying for a butch. You can also consider financially teaming up with friends to bid on a particular service.

Due to limited venue capacity, please let us know if you're no longer able to attend so we can offer your spot to someone else.

During the Auction -

Our MCs will introduce each butch, what they're offering, and a reminder of the butch's terms and conditions before opening the floor to bids. 

At the end of the bidding, the contact details of the top two bidders will be collected.
The full terms and conditions will be shown to the top bidder on the night. They will have 24 hours to decide to accept the T&Cs.

If T&Cs are agreed to -- a group chat between 04BC, bid winner, and the butch will be set up.

If not -- the second top bidder will be notified and be given a chance to review the same T&Cs.

If the second top bidder agrees to the T&Cs -- a group chat between 04BC, bidder and the butch will be set up.

If not -- the offer will not proceed.

After the Auction -

The successful bidder will have a 7-day window to finalise the payment to 04BC.

04BC will facilitate an initial meet and greet between the successful bidder and the butch. This is an opportunity to connect, clarify expectations, and make sure everyone is comfortable with the arrangement before moving forward.

If a disagreement or concern arises, 04BC can help facilitate communication.

If an issue cannot be resolved, or either the butch or successful bidder feels unsafe or uncomfortable proceeding, the offer may be withdrawn. Any refund considerations will be assessed in line with the circumstances, but please be aware that a full refund may not be possible as this is a fundraising event.

A VERY IMPORTANT REMINDER


You're bidding on a specific service not purchasing a person.

Winning a bid does not entitle you to anything beyond what the butch has explicitly offered and agreed to. There are no implied romantic, physical or sexual expectations attached to any winning bid.

Every butch has their own boundaries and conditions, and these must be respected throughout the process. Consent is ongoing, and either party can choose not to proceed.

No SWERFs, No TERFs.

Let's keep it cheeky, respectful and safe for everyone ❤️

long_description:
Join us for a special free screening of I Carry It With Me Everywhere by Other Cinemas and The Neglected Miracle by Barry Barclay at Massey University, with kōrero from Arwa Aburawa, Turab Shah, and Hana Pera Aoake on Monday 9 November 6:15pm-9pm.

I Carry It With Me Everywhere was informed by interviews with first-generation migrants living in the UK. This short film weaves together the lives of multiple characters as they confront inherited ideas of belonging. The Neglected Miracle is a film that forms the culmination of five years of international research into the question of who owns our seeds. This involves interviews with corporations, scientists and everyday farmers in the developing world. This was shot over two years in eight different countries. 

We are very lucky to be joined by Turab Shah and Arwa Aburawa of Other Cinemas for a kōrero before the screening. They have come all the way from the UK, so don't miss this chance to hear about the film directly from its makers!

This screening is programmed in concert with the exhibition Unseen. Unheard. Unarchived. by Other Cinemas and Friends, curated by Hana Pera Aoake. The exhibition is on at Enjoy until 19 December.

Snacks and drinks provided!

The screening will be held at Massey Cinema, Old Dominion Museum Building (East entrance): 15 Buckle Street, Mount Cook, Wellington

(Block 10 Tokomaru, Pukeahu Mount Cook, Wellington)

This event is supported by Toi Rauwhārangi College of Creative Arts, Massey University. Enjoy's Public Engagement programme is made possible by the support of Wellington City Council.

Nota Bene presents: Christmas Fantasia

From centuries-old texts to traditional carols given new musical life, this concert explores the many ways composers across different eras and cultures have interpreted the Christmas story.

Our programme brings together music from England to Appalachia, with works by Vaughan Williams, Warlock, Dalglish and Ešenvalds. The music ranges from reflective settings and rich harmonies to folk-inspired carols and familiar Christmas melodies.

Vaughan Williams’ Fantasia on Christmas Carols weaves together traditional English carol melodies, some emerging in the choir and others in the accompaniment. In contrast, Malcolm Dalglish’s Star in the East sets three Appalachian Christmas songs for choir and harp, drawing on a different folk tradition.

Joined by baritone Joe Haddow, harpist Michelle Velvin and organist Rachel Malcolm-Swindells, Nota Bene presents a programme that moves between familiar carols and less familiar musical settings.

And what better way to finish than by singing some favourite Christmas carols together? As is our tradition, we hope you’ll stay and join us for refreshments after the concert.

Rachel Malcolm-Swindells - Organ

Michelle Velvin - Harp

Joe Haddow - Baritone

long_description:
About the training

This immersive training invites you to awaken the subtle body through the practice of yoga. The subtle body is the energetic field that connects body, breath and mind.

Over the course of this 3-day training, we explore how movement, breath and awareness shape the flow of prana. Through asana, pranayama and meditation, you will deepen your connection to the more subtle layers of your practice and refine how you move, breathe and sequence with intention.

What you will explore

The foundations of yoga energetics including prana, nadis, bandhas and chakras

the relationship between physical alignment and the energetic flow

Sequencing as a tool to guide prana through the body

Pranayama and meditation as gateways to the subtle body

Safe and intelligent progressions toward more advanced postures

Any questions? Head to our FAQ at the bottom of the page.

SCHEDULE

The training is 3 full days with each day designed to lead on to the next. Lunch break is from 12-1:30pm.

Friday 9am - 4pm - Sequencing towards arm balances

We explore sequencing as a roadmap for practice and learn how arm balances support lightness, strength and flow. Themes include prana, the five koshas, bandhas and biomechanics as a gateway to the subtle body. The day ends with pranayama practice.

Saturday 9am - 4pm - Sequencing towards inversions and inner body awareness

A deeper exploration of inversions and their effect on the inner body. We study the nadis and sushumna and how sequencing supports inward awareness. The day closes with restorative postures and meditation.

Sunday 9am - 3:30pm - Sequencing for backbends and subtle body integration

Backbends to uplift prana and access the more subtle layers of practice. We will explore the chakras as the most refined energetic layer and integrate everything through sequencing, meditation, and pranayama. A quiet inward ending to conclude the training.

THE VENUE: BHAKTI LOUNGE

The Bhakti Lounge is located in the heart of Wellington CBD, at level 1, 175 Vivian Street. It has been operating for twenty plus years and is 100% volunteer-run, community first events space.

YOUR TEACHER

Joan Hyman, Senior Yoga Teacher and founder of the School of Yoga (USA)

Joan Hyman is the director and founder of The School of Yoga, an authentic international teacher training program focused on continuing education. Her grounded teaching style seamlessly supports her students as they emerge from their practice with the rich and bright energy that yoga has to offer.

Joan’s teachings come from an organic and intuitive place, as she draws upon the combined studies of Ashtanga and Iyengar yoga as well as Ayurveda and meditation. An authentic modern-day yogi, Joan's love and devotion show up in her practice and throughout her teaching. You will leave her class feeling transformed and deeply aligned.

Joan spent fifteen years as a distinguished YogaWorks Senior Teacher before bringing her expertise to Wanderlust as the Director of Teacher Trainings in 2016. Now, with over twenty years of experience leading retreats, trainings, and international workshops, Joan travels the globe and teaches online, leading her own signature trainings. She has created The School of Yoga, which is a professional education program, helping students and inspiring teachers to work towards their five hundred hours Yoga Alliance Certification. A leader in the yoga community, Joan’s open-hearted approach to teaching yoga keeps both her inner spirit and her students continuously evolving.

YOUR HOSTS

Sarah Marriott and Liz Birkett

Yoga teachers (500YTT) Sarah Marriott and Liz Birkett warmly welcome you! Having studied with Joan Hyman since 2018, they are excited to bring her to Wellington shores once again, so she can share her extensive knowledge of Yoga with Aotearoa's Yoga community. 

FAQ

How much is the 3 day training?

It is $520 (early bird) however this increases to $550 from November 1st, 2026.

Can I attend one or two days?

Sorry, no. This is a 3 day training with each day designed to lead on to the next. Please email Sarah and Liz if you have further questions about this.

Who is this training for?

This training is for dedicated practitioners and teachers who feel curious about the energetics behind the physical practice and who want to deepen their experience beyond alignment alone. This training is open to teachers and dedicated yoga practitioners. You do not need to be a teacher to join. A regular yoga practice and curiosity to dive deeper is enough!

Do I need to bring a yoga mat or any props?

We have mats, and props (blocks, straps bolsters) however you are welcome to bring your own.

Is there parking at the venue?

Street parking:
Best option is to Uber or car pool if you can as street parking is capped at 2 hours (around $5 per hour) during the week and 3 hours (around $3/4) in the weekend.

Car parks:
The Hope Gibbons Parking (68 Taranaki Street) is a 2-3 minute walk from the venue or there are other parking buildings 5 minutes away (E.g., Garrett Street Car Park)

What are the lunch options?

Of course you are welcome to bring your own lunch/snacks. However, there are plenty of cafes and restaurants available to you on nearby Cuba street. You have 1.5 hours for lunch so you may like to dine in, take a drive or head to Oriental Pde for a walk!

The Bhakti lounge also serves a delicious plant-based lunch Mon-Fri at a very affordable price.

I'm from out of town. Is there accommodation nearby?

Yes there are plenty of options just a short walk away.

WELCOME SPACE BROTHERS is a documentary that dives into the extraordinary true story of the Unarius Academy of Science, an extraterrestrial-channeling spiritual school founded in El Cajon in the 1970s. Led by the dazzlingly outlandish Ruth E. Norman—revered as "Archangel Uriel"—Unarius evolved into a wildly inventive public-access television phenomenon. The group produced films that appeared to be elaborately campy space epics yet were, at their core, sincere therapeutic works. 

From The Source Family director Jodi Wille comes another mind-expanding voyage into the wild frontiers of American belief, bringing her singular blend of empathy, humor, and emotional insight to one of the country's most fascinating outsider communities. Produced by Caryn Capotosto (Won’t You Be My Neighbor) and Jodi Wille. Executive producers include Elijah Wood, Moby, and Oscar-winning filmmakers Phil Lord and Christopher Miller.

Please join us for the Wellington screening of WELCOME SPACE BROTHERS - brought to you by Erika Grant and Night Church Cinema. This is a dress up event - come dressed in your favorite UFO/Cult fit. There will be prizes for best dressed, and DJ's Oona Verse and Martyn Pepperell plus others will guide us into the wild starry night with space cult inspired dance tracks.

The bar and restaurant will be open for dinner and drinks. This is a one off event, not to be missed!!

“Wild and Very Trippy” - Jodi Wille

“If I didn’t know Jodi Wille’s film, Welcome Space Brothers, was a documentary, I’d swear it was a WTF, insane, sci-fi tale of weirdness. The story of Ruth is fascinating…..” - Alan NG, Film Threat 

“It’s a vision of healing, acceptance, peace, cooperation, and hope, expressed through an outpouring of unbridled creative energy. If that spells crazy, beam me up!” — Doug Harvey, Artillery

Free Women’s Self-Defence Course: Building Awareness Ahead of the 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence

Empower yourself with practical skills, confidence, and awareness at this free women’s self-defence session, hosted by the National Council of Women of New Zealand (NCWNZ) Wellington Branch in the lead-up to the international 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence campaign (25 November - 10 December).

Delivered in partnership with Wellington Hapkido Academy, this 90-minute workshop offers a supportive space to learn practical personal safety strategies, build confidence, and raise awareness of gender-based violence prevention.

Event Details

Date: Saturday 21 November 2026

Time: 11:00am – 12:30pm

Cost: FREE!!!

Location: Court 3, Club K, 65 Salamanca Road, Kelburn, Wellington

Parking: Available at 65 Salamanca Road, with additional lower-level parking accessible from within the car park.

What You’ll Learn

Awareness and Prevention

- Body language

- Situational awareness

- Risk reduction strategies

Practical Self-Defence Techniques

- Basic strikes

- Escape techniques

- Using everyday objects for self-defence

Scenario Practice

- Practising responses to simulated high-stress situations

What to Bring and Wear

Clothing: Comfortable clothes you can move in

Footwear: Bare feet, as training takes place on mats

Water: Please bring a water bottle

Emergency contact (optional): You may provide a contact name and phone number for use only in the event of a medical emergency. These details will be kept confidential and destroyed afterwards.

Registration and Donations

This session is completely free, and women are warmly encouraged to attend. Bring a friend, learn practical skills, and build your confidence in a supportive environment. Places are limited, so register early to secure your spot!

Optional donations to the NCWNZ Wellington Branch can be made when booking your ticket. Every contribution supports our ongoing advocacy for gender equality, safety, and community wellbeing in Wellington.

Join us for a practical, empowering session ahead of the 16 Days of Activism, helping build confidence and promote awareness of the importance of preventing gender-based violence.

Can no longer attend? If you register but become unwell or are unable to make it, please email wellington@ncwnz.org.nz as soon as possible so someone else can take your place.

long_description:
Much-loved Pōneke blues and roots singer-songwriter Darren Watson is returning to his favourite Lower Hutt intimate venue, The Shed for the third time (with special guest Matt Hay).

For this visit the ex-Chicago Smoke Shop leader, ‘Planet Key’ songwriter, and multiple NZ Music Award nominee is bringing his musical compardre Matt Hay along to both open the show and accompany Watson on harmonica.

Watson’s latest album ‘Darren Watson sings John Hiatt’ was released just over a year ago to critical acclaim, including a 4-star review in US jazz and blues ‘bible’ Downbeat, and spectacular NZ chart success.

Opener Matt Hay’s latest album ‘Dog and Pony Show’ (produced by Watson) was judged ‘Best Americana Album’ at the 2024 Aotearoa NZ Folk Alliance Awards.

“ Matt brings his beautiful songs to open the show and then joins me blowing some beautiful, tasteful harp. I’m really enjoying playing with Matt again.”

Darren says this show, while still featuring a few choice Hiatt covers, will feature more of his own material old and new.

“ I’ve got some new things on the boil, and I’m really enjoying exploring my back catalogue. There’s a surprising amount of songs after forty odd years!.”

For the uninitiated, a Darren Watson show is big on dynamics, foot stomping blues grooves, and emotional pin-drop moments. There’s politics aplenty, and an awful lot of self-deprecating humour.

Watson is well-known as a powerful guitarist but what many people only realise once they hear him live is he can really sing.

Doors open 7pm for a 7.30pm start.

long_description:
The iconic bluesman and one of Australia’s most revered live performers, Lloyd Spiegel, brings his world-famous guitar work, soulful voice, and deeply human storytelling to New Zealand in April 2027!

This is a rare chance to experience world-class artistry up close, in an intimate listening-room setting designed for focus, connection, and a true love of live music.

“A guitarist almost without peer, Spiegel deconstructs how the blues guitar is supposed to operate… makes sweet love to it, then kicks it out the back door.” — Australian Guitar Player

“Spiegel is ALL presence, authority, rhythm and drive. He epitomizes control, soul and passion with white-hot ferocity and blazing instrumental mastery.” — The Age (Melbourne)

📍 Friday 17 April 2027 @ Old St Paul's - Wellington

Seated concert

Doors 7 PM | Show 7:30 PM

Family friendly, with discounted tickets for under 18s

DON'T miss your chance to experience live music at its finest!

ABOUT LLOYD SPIEGEL

Lloyd Spiegel is a travelling bluesman at heart — a guitarist by trade and a storyteller by nature. The 14-time Australian Blues Award winner has spent a lifetime refining a signature style that honours the deep traditions of blues while pushing the music forward in his own unmistakable voice.

His performances move effortlessly between jaw-dropping guitar work, powerful vocals, humour, and deeply human moments, creating shows that feel personal, generous, and completely alive in the room.

With ten albums to his name and an international touring career spanning North America, Europe, Japan, and beyond, Lloyd is equally respected on world-class festival stages and in intimate listening rooms. At home in Australia, he is recognised as a trailblazer for blues music and has been named among the 50 greatest Australian guitarists of all time.

Whether playing to thousands or a quiet, attentive audience, Lloyd Spiegel has a rare gift for connection — making every performance feel like a shared experience, and every listener feel part of the story.

ABOUT THE VENUE

Located in the heart of Wellington, the magnificent Old St Paul’s is one of New Zealand’s most beautiful historic churches, renowned for its stunning timber architecture, soaring vaulted ceilings and warm, intimate atmosphere.

For one special night, Nightingale Concerts transforms this breathtaking heritage landmark into a listening room, bringing audiences together to experience the extraordinary musicianship, stories, and energy of Lloyd Spiegel up close.

Expect an evening of remarkable guitar playing, powerful blues, laughter, and the kind of connection that makes live music so special.

🎟️ Tickets are ON SALE NOW! These intimate concerts have been selling out in venues around the world. With limited seating available, don't miss your chance to experience Lloyd Spiegel live in Wellington!

long_description:
Well Ahead: Put your health on the agenda

An event for women balancing demanding careers, businesses and families, who are already invested in their health and want to understand it more deeply.

As energy, sleep, recovery and body composition shift through midlife, the right information matters.

Well Ahead brings together Dame Susan Devoy and a lineup of experts across health, nutrition, movement and healthy ageing to explore the science and strategy behind:

Energy and recovery

Sleep and stress

Nutrition

Strength and movement

Body composition

Hormonal changes

Perimenopause and menopause

Bone health

Genetics and individual biology

Well Ahead is designed as a connected conversation, not a series of standalone talks.

Each speaker builds on the last, giving you a clearer, more complete picture of your own health rather than a list of disconnected tips.

The day opens with an optional workshop, Your Genes, Your Choices, exploring genetics, DNA testing and the role our genes can play in understanding individual biology. The full programme continues into the afternoon and closes with a live panel and audience Q&A.

Practical information. Expert perspectives. One day, properly invested in your health.

Choose a Morning Workshop pass, Main Event pass, or the Full Pass for the whole day.




Click here to find out more.



“Women spend so much of their lives looking after everyone and everything else. Well Ahead is about putting your own health on the agenda, hearing from people who really know their field, and coming away with information and ideas you can actually use. You don't have to have all the answers. Sometimes you just need to make the time to start asking the right questions.”

- Dame Susan Devoy

Well Ahead is supported by a growing network of organisations across Wellington's business, professional, health, fitness and wellness communities, all helping us bring women together for an important conversation about health through midlife.

About Conquer Health

Conquer Health helps men and women understand their unique biology, so they can focus on what matters to their health today and make informed choices for the years ahead. Rather than one-size-fits-all health advice, Conquer Health combines advanced biological testing with a multidisciplinary clinical team to build a personalised picture of your health, delivered remotely anywhere in New Zealand.
